commit.message:
feat(kanban): hermes kanban clone - reference clones against shared fleet mirrors (t_dad1edd7) (#947)

* feat(kanban): `hermes kanban clone` - reference clones against shared fleet mirrors (t_dad1edd7)

Workers clone fleet repos by hand into scratch workspaces (159 clones on
2026-09-23, 39 of hermes-home, each a full object store). The dispatcher
never clones, so dedupe has to live in a helper the worker calls.

`hermes kanban clone <url> [dest] [-b branch]` runs
`git clone --reference-if-able <root>/mirrors/<owner>/<repo>.git <url>`
for ANG-Ventures/* and Kyzcreig/* GitHub URLs. Mirrors are created lazily
(bare, flock-serialised, tmp+rename so a half-built mirror is never
visible) with gc.auto=0 / gc.pruneExpire=never: a pruned mirror corrupts
every dependent clone. Non-fleet URLs clone normally; a mirror failure
degrades to a plain clone with a stderr warning. `clone` dispatches before
kb.init_db() - it has no board state.

KANBAN_GUIDANCE gains one line pointing workers at the helper (7311 chars,
cap 8000).

Verified:
- tests/hermes_cli/test_kanban_clone.py 15 passed (real git transport via
  url.insteadOf onto local bare repos; alternates present, count-objects
  size 0, never-prune config written, mirror reused, non-fleet plain,
  mirror failure degrades, CLI dispatch never touches kanban.db)
- with test_kanban_tools, test_kanban_cli, test_prompt_builder in a
  scrubbed env: 145 passed, 1 skipped
- live: clone of ANG-Ventures/hermes-home via the helper -> alternates to
  ~/.hermes/mirrors/ANG-Ventures/hermes-home.git/objects, 4.0K objects in
  the checkout (mirror 164M), fsck --connectivity-only clean
- ruff clean

* fix(kanban clone): precious-objects mirrors, forwarded git-clone options, one deletion choke point (t_dad1edd7 r2)

Addresses Argus QA r1 on #947.

B1 test_workspace_deletion_has_one_choke_point: ensure_mirror no longer
calls shutil.rmtree. The mirror is built at a fixed staging path
(<owner>/.<repo>.git.partial) via init --bare + config + fetch and renamed
into place; a failed build is resumed by the next caller instead of deleted.

B3 never-prune: mirrors now get core.repositoryformatversion=1 +
extensions.preciousObjects=true BEFORE the first fetch, so an explicit
`git gc --prune=now` / `git prune` cannot drop objects dependents borrow.
gc.* keys kept as defence in depth. Tests assert literal config values
(not a loop over MIRROR_CONFIG), a behavioural gc --prune=now test with a
precious=False control arm that must corrupt, and the mirror root pinned
to the fleet root under HERMES_HOME=<root>/profiles/<name>.

B5b the helper forwards -q/-v, -n/--no-checkout, --single-branch,
--no-single-branch, --no-tags, --recurse-submodules, --shallow-submodules,
--sparse, -b, -o/--origin, --depth, --filter, --shallow-since,
--shallow-exclude, and accepts `--` before the URL.

C1 URL userinfo is stripped before it is written to the shared mirror's
remote.origin.url. C2 inherited GIT_DIR/GIT_INDEX_FILE/... are scrubbed
from every git subprocess.

Verified (env -i, isolated HOME/HERMES_HOME):
- test_kanban_clone.py + test_kanban_survivor.py: 59 passed
- test_prompt_builder.py + test_kanban_cli.py: 77 passed, 1 skipped
- mutants on copies, all killed: drop preciousObjects (3 fail), drop
  gc.pruneExpire, drop formatversion=1, profile-home mirror root, no
  userinfo strip, no option forwarding (1 fail each)
- KANBAN_GUIDANCE 7360 < 8000; ruff clean

* fix: a --filter clone ignores --reference; never forward/allow that pair (t_dad1edd7 r2)

Measured on the real hermes-home mirror + GitHub (git 2.53.0), objects in
the dependent clone with --reference-if-able <mirror> --no-checkout:
  plain 1.2M | --depth 1 0.7M | --single-branch 0.8M | --filter=blob:none 170M
A partial clone does not borrow from the alternate; it downloads every
object the filter keeps.

kanban clone: with a mirror in use, --filter is dropped with a stderr note
(kept when no mirror). Tests: forwarded-options test asserts 0 own objects
and no partialclonefilter; filter kept without a mirror. 60 passed
(test_kanban_clone + test_kanban_survivor, env -i); mutant keeping the
filter is killed; ruff clean.

* fix(kanban clone): a killed first mirror build never poisons the mirror (t_dad1edd7 r3)

QA r2 R1. r2 built each mirror in a FIXED staging repo that the next caller
resumed. The terminal tool SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs a timed-out command. A
killed git fetch leaves tmp_pack_* files and ref/config locks that git never
reuses. The next build then either promoted that residue into the precious
(unprunable) mirror, or failed every later fetch on the stale ref lock and
degraded to plain clones with rc=0.

Now every build runs in a fresh .<repo>.git.build-<random> staging repo. The
next builder, while holding the mirror flock, discards every dead staging
repo, including the r2 .partial name. The flock is held for the whole build
and the kernel drops it when the builder dies, so any staging repo that
exists under the lock is dead. A build is promoted only if it contains no
tmp_* or *.lock files. A build that fails in-process is discarded before the
error is raised.

_discard_dead_builds is a named, reviewed exception to kanban's
one-deletion-choke-point test. It only touches direct, non-symlink,
realpath-confined children named .<repo>.git.build-* or .<repo>.git.partial,
never a workspace.

Tests (all run the REAL git transport; the kill tests kill REAL helper
subprocesses):
- killed_first_build_never_poisons_the_mirror: 8 terminal-tool-style kills
  (SIGTERM to the group, SIGKILL after 1 s) spread across the build of a
  24 MB / 1,500-branch fixture. After each kill, the next call must clone with
  alternates, leave no residue or staging repo, and produce a mirror no larger
  than 1.05x a clean build. At least half of the kills must land before
  promotion (non-vacuity floor).
- dead_build_residue_is_discarded_not_promoted: .build-* and .partial arms,
  each with tmp_pack, tmp_idx, a ref lock and config.lock.
- discard_only_touches_this_repos_staging: symlink out of the owner dir, and
  symlink to the live mirror inside it.
- K1/MX3: 6 concurrent first clones all get alternates, one mirror.
- K1/MX4: an inherited GIT_INDEX_FILE, or GIT_DIR+GIT_WORK_TREE, leaves the
  victim's index and config byte-identical.
- K2: precious + pruneExpire are already set when the fetch runs.

Verified:
- clone + survivor + kanban_cli: 77 passed. ruff clean.
- Mutants, each on its own worktree: 8/8 killed. MX3 no flock, MX4 no env
  scrub, MX1 config after fetch, no discard on entry, no residue check, no
  symlink guard, and the r2 source itself (born-red: 3 failed).
- Real path, real GitHub, ANG-Ventures/hermes-home, sandbox mirrors root,
  terminal-tool kills at 2 / 4.5 / 5 / 7 s. Each kill left a 5.9-132 MB
  tmp_pack in its own staging repo. Each next call returned rc=0 with no
  warning and promoted a residue-free precious mirror of 169,168-169,948K,
  against 169,420K for a clean build. Each dependent had 4K of its own
  objects and fsck 0.

---------

Co-authored-by: Apollo <apollo@angventures.io>

* fix(kanban clone): a killed first mirror build never poisons the mirror (t_dad1edd7 r3)

QA r2 R1. r2 built each mirror in a FIXED staging repo that the next caller
resumed. The terminal tool SIGTERMs then SIGKILLs a timed-out command. A
killed git fetch leaves tmp_pack_* files and ref/config locks that git never
reuses. The next build then either promoted that residue into the precious
(unprunable) mirror, or failed every later fetch on the stale ref lock and
degraded to plain clones with rc=0.

Now every build runs in a fresh .<repo>.git.build-<random> staging repo. The
next builder, while holding the mirror flock, discards every dead staging
repo, including the r2 .partial name. The flock is held for the whole build
and the kernel drops it when the builder dies, so any staging repo that
exists under the lock is dead. A build is promoted only if it contains no
tmp_* or *.lock files. A build that fails in-process is discarded before the
error is raised.

_discard_dead_builds is a named, reviewed exception to kanban's
one-deletion-choke-point test. It only touches direct, non-symlink,
realpath-confined children named .<repo>.git.build-* or .<repo>.git.partial,
never a workspace.
